assign.now: Q3 landed - tag hygiene applied over all 47 records; moving to the numbers, the scan gap and the two unfinished records

log.msg: Q1 the newcomer test, shot headless at 400 and 1920 (six pages, zero console errors). /websites/ and /websites/tag/2-sidebar/ PASS - the first sentence says what the page is and the wall is the proof. A SITE page FAILS twice: (1) nothing anywhere said the four thumbnails are the same page at four window widths, so a stranger met four unlabelled pictures and a row of jargon; (2) the url slug in the h1 is a bare <small>, which only steps one notch down from its PARENT - at 400 nytimes-home read as a second h1 and pushed the first picture off the screen. Fixed both in Site.js/Site.css.

Q2 eight records sampled against their own shots (nike-home, amazon-kindle-product, hacker-news-home, gov-uk-home, arstechnica-home, apple-home, ikea-home, css-tricks-home). Four are exactly right (hacker-news, gov-uk, ikea, css-tricks - gov-uk measures 480..1440 in a 1920 window, which is 960 centred, as claimed). FOUR were wrong at a width: nike-home 400 said 4-1 where the shot is six EQUAL tiles two across; amazon-kindle-product 400 said 2-sidebar where the shot is the DESKTOP page running off the right edge (search box cut mid-word) - it never responded, so all four widths are 3-holy-grail; apple-home said 1-flow/1-centered while its own strategy sentence said 1-bands, and the shots are a stack of full-bleed colour bands at every width; arstechnica-home said 2-sidebar for two tracks its own scan measured at 528px and 576px, an 8% difference, which is 2-equal. All four fixed through the merge.

Q3 tag hygiene: 107 tags -> 52, over 45 of the 47 records, all through tools/lib.mjs write_record. Numbers out of tags (24 max-width NNNN spellings + centred at 1920 + fixed width -> one max-width, 31 sites; 10 hamburger at NNN + bare hamburger -> one hamburger, 25 sites) - the width itself is still in responsive.breakpoints and in the prose. Retired ids folded to what layouts.json defines (3-cards->3-equal+cards, 4-equal and card wall->n-wall, bento and mosaic->4-1). Sides folded to left/right, toc variants to toc, full-bleed art/video to full-bleed, float infobox to float. Capture notes dropped from the tag row (bot wall, cookie modal, gallery-find, right-aligned) - every one of them is already a sentence in that record notes, checked. Category spelled one way: docs and reference -> documentation (8); gallery-find was where the scout FOUND the site, not what it is, so its six were re-read from their own first sentence (5 marketing, 1 shop). Now 41 of 52 tags are shared by two or more sites; it was 55 of 107.

Q4 the numbers, counted independently in Node over the 47 records on disk (not from index.json, not by the page code): 21 one-column at 1920, 16 two, 8 three, 2 four = 47; at 400, 37 are 1-flow, 10 are not, 8 of those 10 are still a single column, so exactly 2 keep a second column on a phone (amazon-kindle-product 3-holy-grail, nike-home 2-equal). The headline on /websites/patterns/ prints the same eight numbers because it counts them at render. Bars are readable at 400 - shot and looked at (websites-patterns-400.jpg). The only change my fixes made to the page is that it is now honest: no alias arrows are drawn, because no record spells an alias any more.

Q5 the tool gap, fixed and proved. scan.mjs measure() returned inline_css_BYTES - a number - so the inline style TEXT never crossed the page boundary and the @media regex ran over the wire sheets alone. Any Framer-built site therefore read as 0 stylesheets AND 0 media queries (privy-home: 286241 inline bytes, zero queries). measure() now returns the text itself, deduplicated across the four loads, and scan.css reports inline_blocks beside sheets. Proved LOCALLY, no internet: a file:// page with one inline style block and no stylesheet scanned as 0 sheets + 1 inline blocks / 549 bytes, 3 media queries and 1 container query, all four correct; the throwaway record was deleted. Written up in doc/tools.md with the signature of a record scanned before the fix (css.sheets 0 with a big inline_bytes).

Q6 the two unfinished records. The briefs premise was already stale: python-docs-index has all five jpegs on disk, so nothing was missing to placeholder. The robustness fix was made anyway because it is real - Site.shot() now draws every one of the four widths and marks the figure .is-missing when the record names no path OR the img fails to decode (the SPA answers a missing .jpg with index.html at 200, so only the error event can catch that), and Site.css swaps the picture for a dashed box saying not captured at NNN px. Proved by aborting mdn-css/1920.jpg headless: exactly one figure went .is-missing, zero broken images (proof-missing-shot.jpg). Both records now have a wire, written from the 1920 and 400 shots: django as SHARES (69/31, because its float split holds that ratio at every width) with its two coloured bands above and its five-column footer below, python as two MEASURED tracks that do not fill the row, so the drawing leaves the dead strip on the right that is the whole point of that record. 47 of 47 records now carry a wire.

Q7 the blog leftovers. blog/readme.md gained the Watch out line: meta.mjs reads the card size out of a PNG IHDR at bytes 16 and 20, Node core only, so a .jpg in image:/card_image: ships with no og:image:width or height. imagine/research/page.js question: now covers all five topics (it said ancient technology only; the description beside it already said five). /blog/ai/playwright/ PASSES the newcomer test at both widths with no edit: the first screen is the title, one sentence saying what the post covers, then a plain paragraph that explains Playwright to someone who has never heard of it, then a picture of this very site shot by a browser nobody opened. post.md untouched, so meta.mjs was not re-run.

Verification: 108 pages crawled headless at 1280 (/websites/, patterns, best, every doc note, all 52 tag pages, all 47 site pages). Zero console errors from our own code, zero .md-error boxes, zero broken images, no empty pages. The one flagged line is a CSP warning emitted by the live embedded m3.material.io iframe on material3-home, which capture-c logged when it landed.

Deliberately left. (1) core Page title CSS breaks a long word at 400 - 3.14.7 Documentatio/n on python-docs-index - which is core/Page, outside this brief fence and true of every long-titled page on the site. (2) responsive.queries strings still carry a trailing brace from scan.mjs regex; fixing the regex would make new records disagree with the 47 already scanned, and nothing renders the strings (the site page shows only the count). (3) Singleton trait words (layout switcher, minimal, no gap, ...) were KEPT: a one-site word is the vocabulary the second site will match, and the front row already hides both ends.

assign.outcome:
**Seven questions answered against the pictures, and every fault found was fixed.** [/websites/](/websites/) · [what emerged](/websites/patterns/) · [the tag vocabulary](/websites/doc/tags.md)

![a site page, with a width we did not photograph drawn as a plain box instead of a broken image](proof-missing-shot.jpg)

- **The newcomer test.** The front and the tag pages pass. A SITE page failed twice and both are fixed: nothing said the four thumbnails were the same page at four window widths (there is now one plain sentence above them), and the url slug in the heading was a bare `small`, which only steps one notch down from its parent — at 400 it read as a second title and pushed the first picture off the screen.
- **Eight records, sampled against their own shots.** Four were exactly right; four were wrong at a width and are corrected: `nike-home` at 400 (six equal tiles two across, not a mosaic), `amazon-kindle-product` at 400 (the desktop page running off the right edge — it never responded), `apple-home` (its own strategy sentence said `1-bands` while its layout map said `1-flow`), `arstechnica-home` (528px beside 576px is `2-equal`, not a sidebar).
- **Tag hygiene: 107 tags → 52**, across 45 of the 47 records, all through `tools/lib.mjs`. Numbers out of tags (24 `max-width NNNN` spellings → one `max-width`; 10 `hamburger at NNN` → one `hamburger`), retired ids folded to what `layouts.json` defines, capture notes moved out of the tag row and into `notes`, one spelling per category. 41 of 52 tags are now shared by two or more sites; it was 55 of 107.
- **The numbers hold.** Counted independently in Node over the records on disk: 21 one-column at 1920, 16 two, 8 three, 2 four; only 2 of 47 keep a second column at 400. [The page](/websites/patterns/) prints the same eight because it counts them at render, and the bars are readable at 400.
- **The scan gap is closed.** `measure()` returned the inline CSS *byte count*, so the `<style>` text never crossed the page boundary and any Framer-built site read as 0 stylesheets and 0 media queries. It now returns the text. Proved on a local file with one inline block and no stylesheet: 3 media queries and 1 container query, all correct.
- **47 of 47 records now carry a wire**, and a missing shot can never render as a broken image — every width keeps its slot and draws a dashed "not captured" box instead.
- **The blog leftovers:** the PNG-only card rule is a Watch out line in [`blog/readme.md`](/blog/readme.md), the research front's question covers all five topics, and [the post](/blog/ai/playwright/) passes the newcomer test at 400 and 1920 with no edit.

108 pages crawled headless: zero console errors from our own code, zero broken images, zero `.md-error`.

**Left, with reasons.** Core's page-title CSS breaks a long word at 400 (`Documentatio/n`) — that is `core/Page`, outside this fence and true of every long-titled page. `responsive.queries` strings keep a trailing brace — fixing the regex would make new records disagree with the 47 already scanned, and nothing renders the strings. Singleton trait words were kept: a one-site word is the vocabulary the second site will match.
